hypothesis: Question: the parent (idea-ae78bf, action 8305d9ba...) kept the baseline HGB (squared branch selected; dev RMSE 59.976 vs baseline 59.993, effectively unchanged) and showed forward-holdout RMSE far worse than development (fold1 days 424-485: 116.6; fold2: 74.9). Tree models predict a flat level beyond the training day range, so a continuing 2011->2012 growth trend cannot be extrapolated by elapsed_day/yr splits; the log1p and poisson branches, which encode multiplicative structure, were nevertheless worse on those forward folds, so a pure loss change is not the fix. This program tests a separable trend: fit log daily totals on training dates only as a + b*day + two day-of-year harmonics, deflate the target by exp(b*(day-last_train_day)), fit the same fixed-hyperparameter squared-error HGB on the deflated target, and re-inflate predictions with the extrapolated factor. Two deflated variants (drop yr/elapsed_day so the trend must live in the deflator; keep all features) are compared with the unchanged squared branch using the parent's two forward 61-day holdouts, with b re-estimated inside each fold. Contrasting expected outcomes: (A) if the level shift is a persistent exponential trend, deflated branches cut forward-fold RMSE materially (fold1 well below 116) and the program selects a deflated branch, giving dev RMSE below 59.98; (B) if growth has saturated or is seasonal confounding, the deflator over-predicts, deflated branches lose on forward folds, the program keeps 'squared' and the dev result matches the parent, an informative negative result about trend transfer. Findings expose the estimated daily growth rate and implied annual factor per fold and for the final refit, so the selected branch and its trend assumption are visible. Note the branch selection is by forward-holdout RMSE only; a 5% dev gain from this single 61-day period would still not establish transfer to July-December. Unverified until executed.
